proposals.before: In the second year, when the Khitans invaded the south, he accompanied the court to Chanzou. At the northern crossing of Yan prefecture the Khitan force was routed and thousands drowned. For this he was appointed military governor of Hua.
proposals.after: In the second year, when the Khitans invaded the south, he accompanied the court to Chanzhou. At the northern crossing of Yun prefecture the Khitan force was routed and thousands drowned. For this he was appointed military governor of Hua.
proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou, not Chanzou; 鄆州 is Yunzhou, not Yan prefecture.

proposals.before: In the second year, when the Khitans raided south, he followed the emperor to Chanzou; at the northern ford of Yanzhou the Khitan army was utterly defeated and several thousand drowned; for this merit he was appointed military governor of Huazhou.
proposals.after: In the second year, when the Khitans raided south, he followed the emperor to Chanzhou; at the northern ford of Yunzhou the Khitan army was utterly defeated and several thousand drowned; for this merit he was appointed military governor of Huazhou.
proposals.reason: Same toponym errors: 澶州 and 鄆州 are misread as Chanzou and Yanzhou.

proposals.before: The next day, traveling to Zhao Commandery, he moored at the county seat and said to his attendants, "I have not eaten for two nights; my illness is severe. When the lord is shamed, the minister dies — I shall go no farther south."
proposals.after: The next day, traveling to Zhao Commandery, he lodged at the county seat and said to his attendants, "I have not eaten for two nights; my illness is severe. When the lord is shamed, the minister dies — I shall go no farther south."
proposals.reason: 泊其縣舍 means lodging at the county hostel, not mooring a boat.

proposals.before: When Emperor Gaozu of Han took the throne, an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Director of the Department of State Affairs.
proposals.after: When Emperor Gaozu of Han took the throne, an edict posthumously honored him as Director of the Department of State Affairs.
proposals.reason: 詔贈 is a posthumous honorific appointment, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: In the first month of the third year of Guangshun under the Zhou, Huang Fuyu's wife, Lady Huo of the State of Song, petitioned to be ordained as a nun. Emperor Taizu of Zhou granted it, bestowed purple robes upon her, gave her the title Great Master of Chaste Exemplar and the religious name Huiyuan, and granted ten summer offerings as well.
proposals.after: In the first month of the third year of Guangshun under the Zhou, Huang Fuyu's wife, Lady Huo of the State of Song, petitioned to be ordained as a nun. Emperor Taizu of Zhou granted it, bestowed purple robes upon her, gave her the title Great Master of Chaste Exemplar and the religious name Huiyuan, and granted ten years of monastic seniority as well.
proposals.reason: 夏臘 counts ordained summer-retreat years of seniority, not summer offerings.

proposals.before: His father Du for generations were farmers.
proposals.after: His father Du had been farmers for generations.
proposals.reason: Literal English treats the singular father as a plural verb phrase; the Chinese says the father came of generations of farmers.

proposals.before: In the second month of the second year of Kaiyun he followed Du Chongwei on the northern expedition, lifted the siege of Yangcheng, and was promoted to honorary Minister of Works.
proposals.after: In the third month, in spring of the second year of Kaiyun, he followed Du Chongwei on the northern expedition, lifted the siege of Yangcheng, and was promoted to honorary Minister of Works.
proposals.reason: Chinese 春三月 is the third lunar month in spring, not the second month.

proposals.before: In the second month of the second year of Kaiyun he followed Du Chongwei on the northern expedition, lifted the siege of Yangcheng, and was promoted to honorary Minister of Works.
proposals.after: In the third month of spring of the second year of Kaiyun he followed Du Chongwei on the northern expedition, lifted the siege of Yangcheng, and was promoted to honorary Minister of Works.
proposals.reason: Chinese 春三月 is the third lunar month; both English fields wrongly say second month.

proposals.before: In the seventh year he was transferred to honorary Minister of Works and given nominal charge of Lang prefecture as militia training commissioner.
proposals.after: In the seventh year he was transferred to honorary Minister over the Masses (Situ) and given nominal charge of Lang prefecture as militia training commissioner.
proposals.reason: Chinese 檢校司徒 is Situ, not 司空 (Minister of Works), which was already used in the previous sentence.

proposals.before: In the seventh year he was transferred to honorary Minister of Works and held Lang Prefecture militia training commissioner in nominal charge.
proposals.after: In the seventh year he was transferred to honorary Minister over the Masses (Situ) and held Lang Prefecture militia training commissioner in nominal charge.
proposals.reason: Literal English repeats Minister of Works for 司徒; 司徒 is not 司空.

proposals.before: In the eighth year he was appointed defense commissioner of Chen prefecture. Returning from Chanzou with the Young Emperor, he was made honorary Grand Guardian and defense commissioner of Zheng prefecture, appointed commander-in-chief of the Palace Horse Guard, soon given military commissioner of the Yongqing Army, and shortly afterward confirmed as full military governor.
proposals.after: In the eighth year he was appointed defense commissioner of Chen prefecture. proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou, not Chanzou; 兵馬留後 is an acting retainee posting, not yet full military commissioner.

proposals.before: In the eighth year he was appointed defense commissioner of Chen Prefecture; returning from Chanzou with the Young Emperor, he was changed to honorary Grand Guardian and defense commissioner of Zheng Prefecture, appointed commander-in-chief of the Palace Horse Guard, soon removed as military commissioner of the Yongqing Army, and shortly afterward given full appointment as military governor.
proposals.after: In the eighth year he was appointed defense commissioner of Chen Prefecture; returning from Chanzhou with the Young Emperor, he was changed to honorary Grand Guardian and defense commissioner of Zheng Prefecture, appointed commander-in-chief of the Palace Horse Guard, soon appointed military commissioner-retainee of the Yongqing Army, and shortly afterward given full appointment as military governor.
proposals.reason: 除 means to appoint, not to remove; 澶州 is Chanzhou.

proposals.before: That year an edict ordered him to lead a thousand cavalry to garrison Ji prefecture. He met five thousand Khitan cavalry at the northern border of Fuyang and fought bitterly all day. Outnumbered, he was struck by a stray arrow and died in the line — it was the eleventh month of that year; he was forty-nine.
proposals.after: That year an edict ordered him to lead a thousand cavalry to garrison Ji prefecture. Outnumbered, he was struck by a stray arrow and died in the line — it was the eleventh month of that year; he was forty-nine.
proposals.reason: 淤口關 is Yukou Pass; Yankou does not match 淤.

proposals.before: That year an edict ordered him to lead a thousand cavalry to garrison Ji Prefecture; soon, with Du Chongwei's northern campaign, an edict appointed Hanzhang chief array marshal of the northern horse army, dispatched to recover Yankou Pass; he met five thousand Khitan cavalry at the northern border of Fuyang; they fought bitterly all day; because the numbers were unequal he was struck by a stray arrow and died in the battle line — it was the eleventh month of that year; at the time he was forty-nine years old.

proposals.before: That month his son Hairong presented Hanzhang's riding whip, horse, and weapons and armor; the emperor grieved and wrote a posthumous enfeoffment as Grand Commandant.
proposals.after: That month his son Hairong presented Hanzhang's riding whip, horse, and weapons and armor; the emperor grieved and posthumously honored him as Grand Commandant.

proposals.before: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he was summoned to court, promoted beyond the usual to honorary Minister of Works, appointed commander of the left wing of the Imperial Guard, and given nominal charge of She prefecture.
proposals.after: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he was summoned to court, promoted beyond the usual to honorary Minister over the Masses (Situ), appointed commander of the left wing of the Imperial Guard, and given nominal charge of She prefecture.
proposals.reason: 檢校司徒 is Situ, not Minister of Works (司空).

proposals.before: When Gaozu ascended the throne he was summoned to court and promoted beyond the usual to honorary Minister of Works, appointed commander of the left wing of the Imperial Guard, and held She Prefecture in nominal charge.
proposals.after: When Gaozu ascended the throne he was summoned to court and promoted beyond the usual to honorary Minister over the Masses (Situ), appointed commander of the left wing of the Imperial Guard, and held She Prefecture in nominal charge.

proposals.before: When Siyuan was military governor of Yan prefecture, he led his troops to encamp at Desheng Crossing and left Shunmi to defend the city. proposals.after: When Siyuan was military governor of Yun prefecture, he led his troops to encamp at Desheng Crossing and left Shunmi to defend the city. proposals.before: Zhuangzong believed him and soon dispatched Mingzong to lead the army toward Yan; they indeed took it — this was due to Shunmi's original plan.

proposals.before: Shunmi by nature was sincere and generous; in commanding armies and comforting the people, he all had a reputation for benevolence.
proposals.after: Shunmi by nature was sincere and generous; in commanding armies and comforting the people, he had a reputation for benevolence.

proposals.after: Emperor Gaozu deeply mourned him and posthumously honored him as General-in-Chief of the Valiant Guard.

proposals.after: Emperor Gaozu, hearing that Gui had met with disaster, sighed for a long time and issued an edict posthumously honoring him as Grand Tutor.

proposals.after: Gaozu, hearing that Gui had met with disaster, sighed for a long time and issued an edict posthumously honoring him as Grand Tutor.

proposals.before: In the third year of Tongguang he followed the Prince of Wei Jiji in pacifying Shu. When Kang Yanxiao rebelled, the Prince of Wei appointed Yun chief adjutant of horse and foot for the expedition; he led troops with Ren Yuan to strike Yanxiao at Han prefecture and captured him to present. Before merit could be recorded, Mingzong ascended the throne.
proposals.after: In the third year of Tongguang he followed Jiji, the Prince of Wei, in pacifying Shu. When Kang Yanxiao rebelled, the Prince of Wei appointed Yun chief adjutant of horse and foot for the expedition; he led troops with Ren Yuan to strike Yanxiao at Han prefecture and captured him to present. Before merit could be recorded, Mingzong ascended the throne.
proposals.reason: 魏王繼岌 is Jiji, Prince of Wei; “Prince of Wei Jiji” fuses the title and given name as if Wei were a surname.

proposals.before: In the third year of Tongguang he followed Prince of Wei Jiji in pacifying Shu; when Kang Yanxiao rebelled, the Prince of Wei appointed Yun as chief adjutant of horse and foot for the expedition, leading troops with Ren Yuan to strike Yanxiao at Han Prefecture and capture him to present; before merit could be recorded, Mingzong ascended the throne.
